frame.grid.note: 64x64 luminance grid; compared with a TOLERANCE, never byte-wise, because llvmpipe is not bit-reproducible across runs

frame_control.control_method: the IDENTICAL scenario - same staging, same world, same ticks, same dump - run with --blank-screen, i.e. the same mission screen opened with NO background image, so the ONLY variable is whether the decoded PNG reaches the screen. The image-absent run recorded png_texture_uploads=[] , which is the independent, non-graphical confirmation that the backdrop is decoded ONLY when the screen asks for it.
frame_control.tolerance_source: tests/golden/frame_hash.py derive_tolerance() over tests/golden/calibration.json (bead oo-ae9; noise floor 0.002541, weakest real signal 0.007541). USED AS MEASURED, never adjusted.
frame_control.verdict: the frame moves 0.138777 (31.7x the tolerance) when the decoded PNG is absent, while two independent launches of the real scenario differ by 0.000531 (0.121x). A 261-fold separation, both values well inside bead oo-ae9's measured discrimination band.

landing_rehearsal.note: both the gate and the offline tests search goldens/windows-x64/010-png-test-suite/ FIRST and fall back to tests/golden/pending/010-png-test-suite/, so landing is a pure `git mv` with no code change. See LANDING.md.

stability.note: 10/10 runs exited 0 and wrote a BYTE-IDENTICAL dump. The frame grids are all distinct, as expected: llvmpipe is not bit-reproducible, which is why the grid is compared with the measured tolerance and is NOT part of state.json.
